en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on the Taintless:
Are all phenomena of an Arahant taintless? Yes.
Is the path, the fruit, and Nibbāna; the stream-entry path and the fruit of stream-entry; the once-return path and the fruit of once-return;

the non-return path and the fruit of non-return; the arahant path and the fruit of arahantship; and the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment [identical]?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that all phenomena of an Arahant are free from taints? Yes.
Is the eye of an Arahant free from taints?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is the eye of an Arahant free from taints?
“Yes,” you say.
“The path, the fruit, and Nibbāna; the stream-entry path, the stream-entry fruit … [and so on] … the enlightenment factor”—is this what you mean?
You should not speak thus … [and so on].
The ear of the Arahant … the nose of the Arahant … the tongue of the Arahant … [and so forth].
Is the body of an arahant free from taints?
One should not say so …pe… Is the body of an arahant free from taints?
“Yes,” [you say].
“The path, the fruit, and Nibbāna; the stream-entry path, the stream-entry fruit … [and so on] … the enlightenment factor”—is this what you mean?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …”
Is the body of an Arahant free from taints? Yes.
Is the body of an Arahant subject to exertion and restraint, subject to cutting and breaking, and common to crows, vultures, and hawks?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is a state free from taints (anāsava-dhamma) one that is subject to encouragement and suppression, subject to cutting and breaking, and common to crows, vultures, and hawks?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … .
“Could poison affect the body of an Arahant? Could a weapon affect it? Could fire affect it?”—“Yes.
“Could poison affect an untainted state (dhamma)? Could a weapon affect it? Could fire affect it?”—“No.”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … It is possible to bind the body of an arahant with a leather thong, to bind it with a rope, to bind it with a chain,
to bind it to a village, to bind it to a town, or to bind it to a city.
To bind, to bind with the bonds of the countryside, or to bind with the fivefold bonds including the neck?
Yes, [you say].
Is it possible to bind a state free from taints (anāsava-dhamma) with the bond of a leather thong, to bind it with the bond of a rope, or to bind it with the bond of a chain? [No.]
To bind him, to bind him with the bonds of villages, market towns, cities, and provinces, or to bind him with the fivefold bonds including the neck?
One should not say so… [as before]… If an Arahant gives a robe to an ordinary person (puthujjana), does it become subject to the taints (sāsava) after having been free from the taints (anāsava)?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that having been without taints (anāsava), it becomes with taints (sāsava)? Yes.
Is that which is itself untainted (anāsava) also tainted (sāsava)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is that which is itself untainted also tainted?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then does the path, having been without outflows (anāsava), become with outflows (sāsava)?
One should certainly not say so …pe…
The fruit … the foundation of mindfulness … the right effort …
The basis for spiritual power … the faculty … the power …
“Does a factor of enlightenment, having been free from taints (anāsava), become possessed of taints (sāsava)?

One should not say so… [as before]… If an Arahant gives alms-food to an ordinary person (puthujjana), gives lodging, or gives medicinal requisites for the sick, does that which was free from taints become possessed of taints?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that one who was without taints becomes possessed of taints? Yes.
Is that which is itself without taints (anāsava) also with taints (sāsava)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is that which is itself without taints also with taints?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does the path, having been without taints (anāsava), become with taints (sāsava)?
[The respondent replies: “One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
The fruit … the foundation of mindfulness … the right effort …
the basis of psychic power … the faculty … the power …
“Does a factor of enlightenment (bojjhaṅga), having been free from taints (anāsava), become possessed of taints (sāsava)?
One should not say so… [as before]… If an ordinary person (puthujjana) gives a robe to an Arhat, does it, having been possessed of taints, become free from taints?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...having been with taints, it becomes without taints? Yes.
Is that which is with taints (sāsava) the same as that which is without taints (anāsava)?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is that which is with taints the same as that which is without taints?
“Yes.
[If so,] does lust, having been with-outflows (sāsava), become without-outflows (anāsava)?
You should not say so …pe…
Is hatred … pe … delusion … pe … and moral shamelessness, having been with taints, become without taints?

It should not be said so … [as before] … If an ordinary person gives alms-food to an Arahant, gives lodging, or gives medicinal requisites for the sick, does he, being with taints, become without taints?
It should not be said so … [as before].
Is it the case that having been with taints (*sāsava*), one becomes without taints (*anāsava*)? Yes.
Is that very same thing which was with taints now without taints?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is that which is with taints (sāsava) the same as that which is without taints (anāsava)? Yes.
Is it the case that lust, having been with taints, becomes without taints?
One should not say so …pe… [the same applies to] hatred …pe…
Delusion … [and so on] … Is it not the case that moral recklessness, having been with taints, becomes without taints?
One should certainly not say so … [and so on].
Is it not to be said that "all states of an Arahant are free from taints"?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that an Arahant is one who is without taints?
Yes, he is.
If an Arahant is indeed one who is without taints, then, indeed, you must say this:
“All phenomena of an arahant are free from taints.
The Discussion on the Taintless is finished.
